title: Which money books should a beginner in India read first?
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: A sensible beginner order: start with The Psychology of Money for the mindset and The Richest Man in Babylon for the saving habit; add Let's Talk Money by Monika Halan for the Indian context on insurance, mis-selling and planning; read The Little Book of Common Sense Investing to understand why low costs and index funds matter; then try I Will Teach You To Be Rich for automation ideas, translating the US details. When you are ready for more, read Thinking, Fast and Slow for biases and chapters 8 and 20 of The Intelligent Investor on Mr. Market and the margin of safety. Treat every book as one author's opinion: check that tax rules, products and returns match India, and be careful with books whose authors sell courses or products.
